text: Read: test 144-164 with its comment; `kMaxBytesPerInputByte` (srb.cpp:28) and its use (71); testdata/fuzz/srb/endless-zeros.srb exists (not opened byte by byte). Name has a comma: side note. 1 Claim: A crafted stream that would inflate zeros forever is refused as "corrupt" quickly, rather than running to the 1 GB cap and failing as "too big". 2 Owner: `srb_inflate_stream*` (srb.cpp:71 guard). Parser only. 3 Real chart: Real input: the bytes are the fuzzer's own `testdata/fuzz/srb/endless-zeros.srb`, pasted in as a literal (L152-155). Claim: refused as corrupt. Owner: miniz plus the guard at srb.cpp:71, independent of the test. The claim is about how the code behaves on this real file; it is checked on the real bytes (a copy of the real file). Speed is not measured (no timing). 4 Direct: L156 the exception message "SRB stream is corrupt." is the one that tells this guard from the 1 GB cap ("exceeds size limit"). L160-162 the player's sentence typed again. 5 Reason: The file's bytes are the real fuzz input. The sentence at 160 as in L130. 6 Display: Display sentence typed (as L130). 7 Failure: Commit 971d30db "srb: a stream that makes bytes from no input is corrupt" names it: a bundle made seconds of zero bytes up to the cap (30 s in the fuzz build). Still possible if the guard is removed. 8 Deleted: L156: guard removed, the stream inflates to the 1 GB cap and throws "exceeds size limit" or hangs (reasoned). L160: plain_error text changes. A fixed order has a 1/720 chance of matching on a second run, so a deterministic test is not possible; say so and ask the user whether the property is worth a test.
